image_description: A close-up, angled view of a transparent plastic audio cassette tape. The internal mechanism, including black spools and reddish-brown magnetic tape, is visible through the clear casing. A white paper label with handwritten text ('50', '15/2') is affixed to the top face. A pink rectangular sticker or insert is visible on the left side. The cassette rests on a plain, light-colored surface.

artifact_observations.location: Right side of the cassette casing
artifact_observations.reasoning: The plastic texture on the right side appears slightly 'waxy' or overly smooth with inconsistent specular highlights compared to the sharper reflections on the left. There is a slight lack of fine surface detail (scratches/dust) expected on real plastic.
The internal spool teeth/hubs appear slightly irregular and non-uniform in their circularity, suggesting minor geometric warping common in AI generation of complex mechanical internals.

The handwriting on the label is stylized and somewhat ambiguous. While it resembles numbers ('50', '15/2'), the strokes lack the precise pressure variation of real ink, appearing slightly 'painted' rather than written.

To check if the internal spools are correctly positioned behind the transparent front layer and not floating or merged with the casing.

Geometric correctness of internal spool mechanisms

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the internal mechanics. AI often fails to render the complex interlocking teeth of cassette spools correctly. Check if the spools look like functional mechanical parts or just vague circular shapes. Also, evaluate the 'handwriting' on the label – does it look like genuine ink on paper, or does it have the smeared/painted look of AI-generated text?
